proof.criterion: The reviewer's important finding — the daemon-launched controller's GH_CONFIG_DIR is its bundle's first owner's directory, because its launch names no repository, and not "the project's default owner's directory".
proof.surface: The derivation executed: appauth.GitHubCredential, the one function every role's gh bundle comes from, called directly with a fake Tokens and owner sets chosen so that "the project's default owner" and "the alphabetically first owner" cannot be the same value. No live surface can settle this clause and none is claimed: this deployment runs `controller: operator`, so no daemon-launched controller container exists, and on INFRA the project's default repository's owner and the first-sorted owner are both `sjawhar` (my own pod's bundle holds exactly two owner directories, /var/run/legion/gh/sjawhar and /var/run/legion/gh/theorem-labs), so a pod read would have agreed with the wrong wording too.
proof.command: A throwaway test file in packages/daemon/internal/appauth calling GitHubCredential(probeTokens{}, func() []string { return owners })(ctx, claim.RoleController, "") for owners {zebra-corp, acme}, {theorem-labs, sjawhar} and {Upper-Case-Owner, mid-owner}, printing bundle.Default and ghconfig.OwnerDir("/var/run/legion/gh", bundle.Default); run with `cd packages/daemon && go test -count=1 ./internal/appauth/ -run TestProbeControllerDefaultOwner -v`, then the file removed (`rm`, then `jj status` reports no change).
proof.observed: owners [zebra-corp acme] -> bundle.Default="acme", GH_CONFIG_DIR=/var/run/legion/gh/acme; owners [theorem-labs sjawhar] -> "sjawhar"; owners [Upper-Case-Owner mid-owner] -> "mid-owner" (the owners are lowercased before the sort, so upper-case-owner sorts last). The first case is the one that matters: `acme` is neither the first listed nor any plausible project default, so the value is the sorted first and nothing else. That is bundle.Default = names[0] over slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(all)) when owner is empty (internal/appauth/credential.go), and the controller's owner is empty because its launch spec carries no repository (controllerSpawnSpec sets no Repository, internal/daemon/specs.go) and gitHubBundles passes l.spec.Repository.Owner() (internal/runtime/sandbox/relaunch.go). GH_CONFIG_DIR is then ghconfig.OwnerDir(GHConfigDir, l.gitHubDefault) (ghAgentEnv, podkind.go) over that default. The sentence now says exactly this, with its reason and its citation.
proof.negativeControl: Two, in the same run. A role whose launch names an owner takes that owner: role implementer with owner "zebra-corp" over the same owner set gives bundle.Default="zebra-corp", GH_CONFIG_DIR=/var/run/legion/gh/zebra-corp — so the empty-owner branch is what produces the sorted first, not a function that answers the same way whatever it is asked. And a controller naming an owner outside the project is refused before anything is minted: `the controller's default owner "outside-corp" is not an owner of the project's repositories`.
